It is submitted, the incident reported is true and it is wrong to say that the allegations made against the revisionst are false,
and/are motivated.
sentences._hearing_file: X Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: Also, reliance has been placed on the findings recorded in the bail rejection orders to submit that the instant revision may be dismissed.
sentences._hearing_file: X Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that the applicant is a juvenile and is entitled to the benefits of the provisions of the Act.
sentences._hearing_file: X Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 June, 2024.json

sentences.text:
Under Section 12 of the Act, the prayer for bail of a juvenile may be rejected 'if there appear reasonable grounds for believing that the release of the juvenile is likely to bring him into association with any known criminal or expose him to moral, physical or psychological danger or that his release would defeat the ends of justice'.
The court has to see whether the opinion of the learned appellate Court as well as Juvenile Justice Board recorded in the impugned judgment and orders are in consonance with the provision of the Act.
sentences._hearing_file: X Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: Section 12 of the Act lays down three contingencies in which bail may be refused to a juvenile offender.
sentences._hearing_file: X Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 June, 2024.json

sentences.text:
These are:-
(i) if the release is likely to bring him into association with any known criminal, or (ii) expose him to moral, physical or psychological danger, or (iii) that his release would defeat the ends of justice?
sentences._hearing_file: X Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: Gravity of the offence has not been mentioned as a ground to reject the bail.
sentences._hearing_file: X Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is not a relevant factor while considering to grant bail to the juvenile.
sentences._hearing_file: X Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: It has been so held by this Court in Shiv Kumar alias Sadhu Vs. State of U.P. 2010 (68) ACC 616(LB).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: X Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: It has been consistently followed in subsequent decisions of this court.
sentences._hearing_file: X Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: Thus, it remains largely undisputed that the applicant - was a juvenile on the date of occurance; does not appear to be prone to criminal proclavity or criminal psychology, in light of the observations of the D.P.O; does not have a criminal history; has been in confinement for an unduly long period of time, in as much as the trial has not concluded within time frame contemplated by the Act.
sentences._hearing_file: X Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: Even otherwise, there does not appear to exist any factor or circumstance mentioned in section 12 of the Act as may disentitle the applicant to grant of bail, at this stage.
sentences._hearing_file: X Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: The father of the applicant undertakes to address the statutory concerns expressed in section 12 of the Act, as to the safety and well being of the applicant, upon his release.

opennyai_summary.13_June_2024__facts:
There is allegation in the FIR against the revisionist that he committed the natural as well as unnatural offence against the daughter of the informant alongwith another co-accused after intoxicating her.
The court below has rejected his bail applicant against the mandate of Section 12 of the Act.
opennyai_summary.13_June_2024__arguments:
Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that it is a case of false implication.
It is submitted, the incident reported is true and it is wrong to say that the allegations made against the revisionst are false,
and/are motivated.
Also, reliance has been placed on the findings recorded in the bail rejection orders to submit that the instant revision may be dismissed.
opennyai_summary.13_June_2024__ANALYSIS:
It is not in dispute that the applicant is a juvenile and is entitled to the benefits of the provisions of the Act.
Under Section 12 of the Act, the prayer for bail of a juvenile may be rejected 'if there appear reasonable grounds for believing that the release of the juvenile is likely to bring him into association with any known criminal or expose him to moral, physical or psychological danger or that his release would defeat the ends of justice'.
The court has to see whether the opinion of the learned appellate Court as well as Juvenile Justice Board recorded in the impugned judgment and orders are in consonance with the provision of the Act.
Gravity of the offence has not been mentioned as a ground to reject the bail.
It is not a relevant factor while considering to grant bail to the juvenile.
It has been so held by this Court in Shiv Kumar alias Sadhu Vs. State of U.P. 2010 (68) ACC 616(LB).
Thus, it remains largely undisputed that the applicant - was a juvenile on the date of occurance; does not appear to be prone to criminal proclavity or criminal psychology, in light of the observations of the D.P.O; does not have a criminal history; has been in confinement for an unduly long period of time, in as much as the trial has not concluded within time frame contemplated by the Act.
Even otherwise, there does not appear to exist any factor or circumstance mentioned in section 12 of the Act as may disentitle the applicant to grant of bail, at this stage.
opennyai_summary.13_June_2024__decision:
Consequently, those orders cannot be sustained.
The order dated 05.04.2024 passed by Additional District & Sessions Judge, Court No.3, Moradabad, in Juvenile Criminal Appeal No. 15 of 2024 (Reena Kumar Vs. State of U.P. and another), and the order dated 29.02.2024 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board, Moradabad, in Case No. 03 of 2024 arising out of Case Crime No. 901 of 2023, under Section 376, 452, 377, 504, 506 of I.P.C, Police Station Majhola,
District- Moradabad whereby Additional District and Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act)
Court No. 3, Moradabad, dismissed the criminal appeal and confirmed the order dated 29.02.2024 passed by Juvenile Justice Board Moradabad, is hereby set aside.
In view of the observations made above, the present criminal revision is allowed.
Let the revisionst,
X-Juvenile S/o Anand Singh, involved in the aforesaid case crime be released on bail, on his furnishing personal bond with two sureties each of like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(i) The revisionist shall not tamper with the evidence or threaten the witnesses;
(ii) The revisionist through guardian shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law;
(iii) The revisionist through guardian shall remain present before the trial Court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence,
without sufficient cause, the trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.
Criminal revision is allowed.
Let the lower court record be returned to the Court below.

opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
The victim was not examined under section 164 Cr.P.C.
The investigating officer of this case was not examined before the trial court.
The Juvenile Justice Board committed error in sending revisionist to special home when he is aged about 40 years now and has no criminal history.
The incident was committed in the year 1999 and therefore there is no justification for sending him to special home at this stage.
10. Learned counsel for the revisionist has further submitted that the appellate court has relied upon section 21 and 22 of the Juvenile Justice Board Act, 1986 and has failed to extend the benefit of Section 15 of Juvenile Justice Board (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000.
He has relied upon the judgment of Apex Court in the case of Jitendra Singh @ Babbo an Another Vs. State of U.P.
reported in 2013 0 Supreme (SC) 620.
11.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
For default of the investigating officer of getting the statement of victim recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C., the entire prosecution case cannot be disbelieved.
The incident took place in the year 1999 and in the year 2025, the investigating officer cannot be found.
There was no reason for falsely implicating the revisionist which has been proved by the witnesses before the trial court.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
The section 16 of the Act, 2000 provides that no juvenile cannot be subjected to death or imprisonment for life and, therefore, the punishment of one and half years awarded to the revisionist is justified and calls for no interference.
14. The revision lacks merit and is, accordingly, dismissed.
15. Keeping in view his age about 40 years, the order of the Juvenile Justice Board dated 08.04.2025 is modified and it is directed that the revisionist shall be sent to jail for carrying out remaining sentence awarded to him as per section 20(2)(ii) of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children)Act, 2015.
The period of custody undergone by the revisionist shall be adjusted.
